_comment: DATA, not code -- update this list as hubs are found to be dead/renamed/replaced, or as new states/hub types are added. Consumed by engine_c.py. `kind` reuses the same source-type taxonomy as the rest of the harness (common.SOURCE_TYPES: debate|forum|interview|questionnaire|guide|voter_pamphlet). `hint` is a query TEMPLATE with <angle-bracket> placeholders (<race/candidates>, <candidate name>, <locality>, <county>, <year>) -- the agent (or, in --dry-run, a best-effort string substitution) fills these in with the actual race's specifics before searching.

global.name: Ballotpedia
global.note: Candidate Connection questionnaire. A candidate having a Ballotpedia page is NOT enough -- confirm the survey was actually completed (the page states this explicitly), not just that the page exists.

global.name: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters)
global.note: LWV's national voter-guide tool. vote411.org and onyourballot.vote411.org frequently return HTTP 403 to fetchers -- rely on search-engine result snippets to judge whether it's filled; an unfetchable page is not the same as a nonexistent one.

global.name: Vote Smart
global.note: Political Courage Test / VoteEasy profile. Many candidates have a page but never answered -- check for actual submitted responses, not just a blank profile.

AZ.name: Citizens Clean Elections Commission
AZ.note: Runs the official general-election debate series plus a voter education guide. Confirm the debate is the current general-election cycle (not a primary or a prior cycle) and which candidates actually participated.

AZ.name: Arizona PBS ("Arizona Horizon" / AZ Votes)
AZ.note: Long-form candidate interviews and election coverage. Check whether comparable candidates in the same race were each given equivalent air time.

AZ.name: KJZZ voter guide
AZ.note: Phoenix-market NPR affiliate voter guide and election coverage.

AZ.name: AZPM
AZ.note: Tucson-market NPR/PBS affiliate. Frequently runs one-on-one interviews and debate coverage -- check both/all candidates got equivalent interviews, not just one side.

OR.name: Oregon Voters' Pamphlet
OR.note: Official state government pamphlet: every candidate's own statement in their own words, distributed to every household. Extremely high-signal when it exists for the race.

OR.name: OPB
OR.note: Statewide NPR/PBS affiliate. Also hosts/covers debates and forums and runs candidate Q&As.

OR.name: Bend Bulletin
OR.note: Central Oregon newspaper of record. Candidate forums, Q&As, and endorsem*nt-adjacent coverage -- check neutrality of the specific piece.

TX.name: Community Impact
TX.note: Runs recurring 'meet the candidates' Q&As covering every candidate in a race with the same questions -- a consistently strong TX local source.

TX.name: Austin Monitor
TX.note: Austin-focused nonprofit local news outlet. Candidate coverage and forum write-ups.

TX.name: KUT
TX.note: Austin NPR affiliate. Voter guides and candidate coverage.

TX.name: local county elections office
TX.hint: "<county> County" elections office sample ballot candidate statements <year>
TX.note: Some TX counties publish official candidate statements or a sample-ballot guide -- check for a per-county elections-office site.

CA.name: LAist / KPCC
CA.note: The dominant neutral local hub in the LA market: runs its own written candidate questionnaire, AirTalk long-form interviews, AND debate coverage/co-hosting -- check all three sub-formats, not just the first hit.

CA.name: Voter's Edge California
CA.note: LWV California / MapLight voter guide tool. Coverage is incomplete for many down-ballot CA races -- confirm a page for THIS specific race actually exists before counting it.

CA.name: League of Women Voters California (state + local chapters)
CA.hint: "League of Women Voters" <locality> California voter guide <race/candidates> <year>
CA.note: Often points to VOTE411 or Voter's Edge rather than hosting its own content directly -- check both the chapter page and where it links.

UT.name: Utah Debate Commission
UT.note: Statewide nonpartisan debate host for major Utah races.

UT.name: KUER
UT.note: Salt Lake City NPR affiliate. Candidate coverage and forums.

local_types.name: local League of Women Voters chapter forum
local_types.hint: "<locality>" League of Women Voters candidate forum <year>
local_types.note: Substitute the race's actual city/county name for <locality>. Often co-moderates with a chamber of commerce or neighborhood association.

local_types.name: local newspaper voter guide / candidate Q&A
local_types.hint: "<locality>" newspaper candidate questionnaire OR voter guide <year>
local_types.note: Substitute the race's actual city/county/paper name. Look for the SAME questions asked of every candidate, not a general profile piece.

local_types.name: local public radio/TV candidate coverage
local_types.hint: "<locality>" public radio OR public television candidate interview <year>
local_types.note: Substitute the race's actual city/region. Check that comparable candidates each got an equivalent interview, not a one-sided profile.

local_types.name: chamber of commerce candidate forum
local_types.note: Substitute the race's actual city/region. Usually neutral/civic but genuinely ad hoc -- confirm it isn't a members-only or endorsem*nt event.

local_types.name: government voter pamphlet / sample ballot
local_types.hint: "<locality>" OR "<county>" voter pamphlet OR sample ballot candidate statements <year>
local_types.note: Substitute the race's actual city/county name. Official government-issued candidate statements are the highest-trust source when they exist.
